balanced.details: Uses gpu_memory_utilization 0.90 (the engine default is 0.92), max_model_len 65,536 tokens (about 100 pages of text), prefix caching on, and performance_mode balanced. Everything else stays at vLLM's defaults, so it suits most chat and coding uses on a card with the model to itself.
balanced.example: 0.90 on a 96 GB card reserves about 86 GB for this engine.
balanced.risks: A model whose own limit is below 65,536 tokens needs a smaller window (vLLM refuses a window above the model's), and a card shared with another engine needs a lower memory share.
balanced.summary: A safe all-round start: 90 % of the card, a 64K-token window and prefix caching.
balanced.when_to_change: Choose it when you are unsure, and adjust one thing at a time from here.

long-context.details: Uses a 262,144-token window (about 400 pages), kv_cache_dtype fp8 to roughly double the tokens that fit in the cache, at most 8 conversations at once, an 8,192-token budget per step, prefix caching and chunked prefill. The attention backend stays on auto; on sm_120 cards forcing FLASH_ATTN with an fp8 cache is refused.
long-context.example: Asking questions about a 300-page report pasted into a single prompt.
long-context.risks: Only models trained for such windows can use it (others are refused or lose quality). fp8 can cost a little answer quality, and few conversations fit at once.
long-context.summary: Fits very long documents: a 262,144-token window with the KV cache stored in 8 bits, for a few conversations at a time.
long-context.when_to_change: Choose it to read whole books, long codebases or big logs in one prompt.

low-latency.details: Uses a 16,384-token window, at most 8 conversations at once, a 2,048-token budget per step so prompts never hold up streaming, prefix caching, async scheduling, performance_mode interactivity and a stream interval of 1 so every token is sent as soon as it exists.
low-latency.example: A single developer chatting with a model and watching the answer stream in.
low-latency.risks: More than a handful of simultaneous users queue up, and prompts above 16K tokens are rejected.
low-latency.summary: Makes one or two users' answers start and stream as fast as possible, with a small window and few conversations at once.
low-latency.when_to_change: Choose it for a personal assistant, a coding helper or a demo where response time matters more than capacity.

max-throughput.details: Sets the memory share to 0.92, shortens the window to 32,768 tokens so more conversations fit in the cache, allows up to 512 conversations at once with a 16,384-token budget per step, turns on prefix caching, chunked prefill and async scheduling, and uses performance_mode throughput. On cards of 70 GiB or more vLLM's own limit is already 1,024 conversations, so there the cap of 512 is a ceiling, not a raise.
max-throughput.example: A shared assistant for a team, answering dozens of requests at the same time.
max-throughput.risks: A single user may see slightly slower answers than with the low-latency preset. The 32K window rejects longer prompts, and 0.92 leaves little room for other programs on the card.
max-throughput.summary: Serves as many users as possible at once, trading longer windows and the fastest single answer for total capacity.
max-throughput.when_to_change: Choose it for a shared service or batch jobs with many simultaneous requests, such as an evaluation run.

reasoning.details: Uses a 131,072-token window, up to 16 conversations at once, prefix caching, chunked prefill, reasoning_parser qwen3, automatic tool choice and tool_call_parser qwen3_xml, the usual pairing for Qwen3.x thinking models. Thinking uses many tokens, so answers take longer and need more window.
reasoning.example: A math or planning question where the model works through steps before the final answer.
reasoning.risks: Parsers for another family can swallow part of the answer or leave raw markup in it. Long thinking raises response time and cache use.
reasoning.summary: Set up for models that think before they answer: a 128K window, the qwen3 reasoning parser and the qwen3_xml tool parser.
reasoning.when_to_change: Choose it for Qwen3-style reasoning models; change both parsers for other families.

tool-agent.details: Uses a 64K window, up to 32 conversations at once, prefix caching (agents resend a growing history each turn), enable_auto_tool_choice and tool_call_parser hermes. The parser must match the model family: hermes suits Hermes models and Qwen2.5-style models; Qwen3.x models need qwen3_xml, gpt-oss needs openai.
tool-agent.example: A coding agent that edits files and runs commands through tool calls.
tool-agent.risks: A parser that does not match the model leaves raw tool markup in the answer and agents stall; the Compatibility check suggests the right one from the model's name.
tool-agent.summary: Set up for assistants that call tools, with automatic tool choice and the hermes parser, and a window that suits agent loops.
tool-agent.when_to_change: Choose it for coding agents or assistants with function calls, and change the parser if your model is not a Hermes-style one.
